Title: Train the AI that spots dumping
Description (plain English): Teach the computer to recognise people, bags, vehicles and dumped waste in camera footage. This happens before the app can detect anything.

Title: Build the app people use
Description (plain English): Everything a user clicks, sees and types: the screens, the buttons, the login, and the engine behind them that stores and serves data.

Title: Set up the servers and make it live safely
Description (plain English): The plumbing that runs the app: the gateway that handles secure web traffic, the video server, the message bus, the database, and how it all starts up on a real machine.

Title: Robot tests that check the app still works
Description (plain English): Automated checks (Playwright) that open the app in a real browser and click through it like a user, so a broken screen is caught before a customer sees it.

Title: Get the customer set up and keep them happy
Description (plain English): Installing at the customer site, adding their cameras and users, training their staff, and checking in after go-live.

Title: Run it reliably on cloud servers, and ship updates safely
Description (plain English): Everything to put the system on cloud machines and keep it running: automated build-and-release, secrets and certificates, backups, monitoring and alerts for the servers themselves, and a safe way to roll out a new version or roll back a bad one.

Title: Connect the customer's real cameras to the system
Description (plain English): At each customer site, find their CCTV cameras, get the right stream address and login for each, confirm the picture comes through, place each camera on the map, and draw the watch-area. This is the bridge between our software and their hardware.

Title: The screens the user sees
Description (plain English): The part of the app that runs in the web browser: every page, button and form the user interacts with.

Title: The engine behind the screens
Description (plain English): The service the screens talk to. It checks who you are, reads and saves data, and answers every request the screens make.

Title: The background helpers
Description (plain English): Programs that run quietly in the background doing scheduled jobs: sending alerts, saving evidence, making reports, health checks.

Title: Prepare the training pictures
Description (plain English): Collect camera frames and mark where the waste, bags, people and vehicles are, so the AI has correct examples to learn from.

Title: The model that finds objects
Description (plain English): The trained model that looks at each video frame and outlines what it sees.

Title: The model that links a person to a bag
Description (plain English): A model that decides whether a person is carrying or dropping a bag, so we know a dump actually happened.

Title: The secure front door
Description (plain English): The single secure entrance to the system. All web traffic goes through it over HTTPS; nothing else is exposed to the outside.

Title: The video server
Description (plain English): Receives the live camera streams and hands them to the app for viewing.

Title: The message bus
Description (plain English): The internal conveyor belt that carries events (like 'a dump was detected') from the detector to the background helpers.

Title: The permanent record
Description (plain English): Where everything is stored for good: cameras, events, alerts, users, evidence records.

Title: The live video analyser
Description (plain English): Watches every camera in real time, runs the detection model on each frame, and raises an event when it sees a dump.

Title: Automatic build and release
Description (plain English): When code is approved, it is automatically built, tested and prepared for release, so deploying is a button press, not a manual chore.

Title: Set up the cloud machines
Description (plain English): Create the servers, network, storage and GPU machine in the cloud in a repeatable way, so the exact same setup can be rebuilt any time.

Title: Keep passwords and HTTPS certificates safe
Description (plain English): Store every password, key and certificate securely, and renew the HTTPS certificate before it expires so the site never goes insecure.

Title: Watch the servers and keep safe copies
Description (plain English): Alert the team if a server is down, disk is full or GPU is overheating, and take regular backups of the database and evidence so nothing is lost.

Title: Ship a new version, or undo it fast
Description (plain English): A safe way to roll out a new version with no downtime, and to go back to the previous version within minutes if something breaks.

Title: List the customer's cameras
Description (plain English): Visit or remotely review the site, list every CCTV camera, and note which ones cover dumping hotspots worth watching.

Title: Get each camera's video into the system
Description (plain English): For each chosen camera, get its stream address and login, and confirm a clear picture reaches the app.

Title: Put cameras on the map and draw where to watch
Description (plain English): Mark each camera's location on the map and draw the exact area on the picture the system should watch for dumping.

Title: Prove it works and hand over
Description (plain English): Run a live test at the site, show the customer a real detection, and get their sign-off that the cameras are correctly connected.

Title: Browser tests for every screen
Description (plain English): Robot tests that sign in, click through each page and confirm what the user should see is actually there.

Title: Login page
Description (plain English): The first screen. The user types their username and password here to get into the system.
Example Flow: User opens the app -> sees the sign-in screen -> types username and password -> presses Sign in -> the dashboard opens.
Expected Outcome: The dashboard opens. Wrong details show a red message: 'Invalid username or password'.

Title: Landing page (Live Monitoring)
Description (plain English): The main screen after signing in. Shows all camera feeds in a grid and live alerts.
Example Flow: User signs in -> camera grid appears -> a dump happens -> that camera lights up and an alert slides in.
Example Payload / Data: Loads camera list and live alerts. No data typed in.
Expected Outcome: Every camera shows live video. New alerts appear without reloading the page.

Title: Analytics page
Description (plain English): Charts and numbers summarising dumping over time, by zone and by camera.
Example Flow: User clicks Analytics -> sees today's count, a 7-day trend and the worst zones.
Example Payload / Data: Reads pre-calculated summaries. Nothing typed in.
Expected Outcome: Charts match the real events. Empty periods show 'no data', not a blank box.

Title: Event History page
Description (plain English): A searchable list of every past dumping event with its photo and video evidence.
Example Flow: User clicks Event History -> filters by zone and date -> opens one event -> views its photo and clip.
Example Payload / Data: Filters sent: zone, date range, severity. Gets back matching events.
Expected Outcome: The list shows only events matching the filters. Each has a photo and a working evidence link.

Title: Settings page
Description (plain English): Where an admin changes how the system behaves: alerts, detection sensitivity, storage, and users.
Example Flow: Admin clicks Settings -> turns on WhatsApp alerts -> changes detection sensitivity -> it takes effect.
Expected Outcome: Each setting is remembered and actually changes what the system does.

Title: Timeline Playback page
Description (plain English): A video-editor-style timeline. Scroll through time to find and replay recorded dumping clips.
Example Flow: User opens Timeline -> drags left to go back in time -> clicks a marker -> the clip plays.
Example Payload / Data: Reads recorded clip markers for the last 3 days.
Expected Outcome: Clips appear as markers on a 24-hour timeline; clicking one plays it. Older than 3 days points to the backup drive.

Title: User Management page
Description (plain English): Where an owner adds admins and an admin adds viewers. This is the only way to create accounts — there is no public sign-up.
Example Flow: Admin opens User Management -> fills name, email, phone, zone -> picks role Viewer -> Save -> the new user gets a set-password email.
Expected Outcome: The new user appears in the list and receives an email to set their own password. An admin can never create another admin.

Title: Find and list the site's cameras
Description (plain English): Walk the site (or use the customer's camera list) and write down every camera, where it points, and whether it covers a dumping spot.
Example Flow: Engineer visits the ward -> notes 14 cameras -> marks 5 that face known dumping corners -> those 5 are chosen for Civilytics.
Example Payload / Data: A simple list: camera name, rough location, points-at-a-hotspot yes/no.
Expected Outcome: A signed-off list of which cameras will be connected.

Title: Get each camera's stream address and login
Description (plain English): For each chosen camera, obtain its RTSP stream link and username/password from the customer's CCTV system (NVR/DVR).
Example Flow: Engineer asks the customer's CCTV vendor -> gets rtsp link + login for each camera -> tests it plays in a video tool before adding it.
Expected Outcome: Every chosen camera has a verified, working stream link.

Title: Add each camera in the app
Description (plain English): Enter each camera's details into Camera Management so the system starts watching it.
Example Flow: Admin opens Camera Management -> Add Camera -> enters name, stream link, picks the zone -> saves -> live video appears.
Expected Outcome: The camera shows live video on the dashboard within a few seconds of saving.
Source: TK-ADDCAM links to frontend Camera Management

Title: Place the camera on the map
Description (plain English): Drop each camera's pin at its real location so it appears correctly on the Camera Map.
Example Flow: Admin opens the camera's settings -> drags the map pin onto the real spot (or types the coordinates) -> saves.
Expected Outcome: The camera appears at the right place on the map. Wrong or swapped coordinates are rejected.

Title: Draw the watch-area on the picture
Description (plain English): On the camera's live picture, draw the exact zone the system should watch for dumping, and set how long someone must linger before it counts.
Example Flow: Admin opens the camera feed -> draws a shape around the dumping corner -> sets 'linger 12 seconds' -> saves -> the detector uses it immediately.
Example Payload / Data: Saves the drawn shape (a polygon) plus the linger-time threshold for that camera.
Expected Outcome: The system only raises dumps inside the drawn area, after the set linger time.

Title: Prove a real detection at the site
Description (plain English): With the customer watching, stage a safe test dump and confirm the system detects it, alerts, and saves evidence.
Example Flow: Engineer places a bag in the watch-area -> waits the linger time -> the dashboard lights up, an alert fires, a clip is saved -> customer signs off.
Example Payload / Data: No data entry; this is a live acceptance test.
Expected Outcome: Customer sees a real detection end-to-end and signs the acceptance form.

Title: Automatic build-test-release on approval
Description (plain English): Set up the automation so that approved code is built, tested and packaged into a release with no manual steps.
Example Flow: A change is approved -> the robot builds it -> runs the tests -> if green, prepares a release image.
Example Payload / Data: Trigger: code merged to the main branch.
Expected Outcome: A ready-to-deploy release is produced automatically; a failed test blocks it.

Title: Auto-renew the HTTPS certificate
Description (plain English): Make the HTTPS certificate renew itself before it expires, so the site is never flagged as insecure.
Example Flow: Certificate nears expiry -> it renews automatically -> the gateway picks up the new one -> users never notice.
Expected Outcome: The padlock in the browser never lapses; renewal needs no human.

Title: Scheduled database and evidence backups
Description (plain English): Take regular, safe copies of the database and the evidence files so a server failure never loses data.
Example Flow: Every night -> the system copies the database and new evidence to secure storage -> keeps copies per the retention rule.
Expected Outcome: A fresh backup exists every day and can be restored in a test.

Title: Alert the team if a server is unhealthy
Description (plain English): Watch the servers themselves (down, disk full, GPU too hot) and message the team when something is wrong.
Example Flow: Disk passes 90% full -> the team gets a message -> they clear space before it fails.
Example Payload / Data: Thresholds for disk, memory, GPU temperature, service up/down.
Expected Outcome: The team hears about a server problem before a customer does.

Title: Zero-downtime deploy with one-click rollback
Description (plain English): Roll out a new version without taking the app offline, and be able to return to the previous version within minutes.
Example Flow: New version deployed -> app stays up -> a bug is spotted -> one command rolls back to the last good version.
Example Payload / Data: Release version number to deploy or roll back to.
Expected Outcome: Updates cause no visible downtime; a bad release is undone in minutes.

Title: Login form
Description (plain English): The two boxes (username, password) and the Sign in button, laid out and working.

Title: Input validation
Description (plain English): Stop the form from submitting until both boxes are filled, and show a clear error if sign-in fails.

Title: Alignment & spacing
Description (plain English): Everything centred and evenly spaced, with the Civilytics logo and company name in place.

Title: Responsiveness
Description (plain English): The page looks right and is usable on a phone, a tablet and a desktop.

Title: UI (look)
Description (plain English): Colours, fonts and the brand mark match the Civilytics style.

Title: UX review
Description (plain English): A person walks through signing in and confirms it feels obvious and quick, with no confusing steps.

Title: Camera grid
Description (plain English): Show all cameras as tiles; let the user switch between 2x2, 3x3 and other layouts.

Title: Live video in each tile
Description (plain English): Play the real camera stream inside every tile.

Title: Alert panel
Description (plain English): A side panel that lists live alerts and lets the user acknowledge them.

Title: Violation highlight
Description (plain English): Make a tile light up when its camera detects a dump; blue when hovered.

Title: Sidebar & navigation
Description (plain English): The left menu that switches between the seven pages, with who is signed in and a sign-out button.

Title: Responsiveness
Description (plain English): On a phone, show one camera plus a list instead of nine tiles at once.

Title: UX review
Description (plain English): A person confirms alerts are noticeable but do not block their work.

Title: Alerts & notifications section
Description (plain English): Toggles for email, WhatsApp and call alerts, each actually saved.

Title: Detection settings section
Description (plain English): A sensitivity slider that really changes how strict the detector is.

Title: Storage & backup section
Description (plain English): Choose where evidence is backed up and for how long it is kept.

Title: Access control section
Description (plain English): A shortcut into User Management and the audit-log switch.

Title: Wire every control to save
Description (plain English): Make each toggle and field actually save and load (today they do nothing).

Title: Remove fake controls
Description (plain English): Delete switches that have nothing behind them (SMS, two-factor, repeat-offender).

Title: UX review
Description (plain English): A person confirms every change they make is remembered and has a visible effect.

Title: Open the live camera picture
Description (plain English): Show the chosen camera's live feed to draw on.

Title: Draw the watch-area shape
Description (plain English): Let the admin draw and adjust a shape around the dumping spot.

Title: Set the linger time
Description (plain English): Enter how many seconds someone must stay before it counts as dumping.

Title: Save and apply live
Description (plain English): Save the shape and time so the detector starts using them straight away.

Title: Confirm on a test
Description (plain English): Watch one detection to confirm the area and timing are right.

Title: Add Camera form
Description (plain English): The form for name, stream link and zone.

Title: Validate the stream link
Description (plain English): Check the link format and that a picture actually comes through before saving.

Title: Show live preview
Description (plain English): Play the camera in the app so the admin confirms it is the right one.

Title: Handle a bad or offline camera
Description (plain English): Show a clear message if the camera cannot be reached, instead of a blank tile.

Title: Login does not fit a phone screen
Description (plain English): The sign-in page was built for desktop only. On a phone the boxes can run off the edge and the bottom can get cut off by the browser bar.
Example Flow: Open the app on a phone -> the Sign in button is partly hidden or the page scrolls sideways.
Expected Outcome: On a 375px-wide phone the whole form is visible with no sideways scrolling.

Title: No way to sign out, and you cannot see who is logged in
Description (plain English): Once signed in there is no sign-out button anywhere, and the screen never shows whose account is in use. On a shared office computer the next person inherits the session.
Example Flow: User finishes their shift -> cannot log out -> walks away -> next person is still signed in as them.
Expected Outcome: A sign-out button and the signed-in name sit at the bottom-left of the menu, on every page.

Title: Camera tile does not light up on a dump
Description (plain English): When a dump is detected the camera tile is supposed to get a coloured border, but a styling conflict means the border never shows.
Example Flow: A dump happens -> the alert arrives -> but the camera tile looks exactly the same as always.
Expected Outcome: The tile that detected the dump shows a clear coloured border at every grid size.

Title: A pop-up covers the whole screen on every alert
Description (plain English): When an alert arrives the panel opens with a dark overlay behind it that blocks everything. During busy periods it keeps stealing the screen.
Example Flow: User is editing a camera's detection area -> an alert fires -> a dark overlay covers their work -> repeats every few seconds.
Expected Outcome: New alerts show without blocking what the user is doing.

Title: Changing a detection setting does nothing
Description (plain English): The Settings page saves a value in the database but never tells the live detector, so the detector keeps using its old setting.
Example Flow: Admin lowers detection sensitivity -> presses Save -> the detector keeps behaving exactly as before.
Expected Outcome: Changing a detection setting changes the live detector within a few seconds.

Title: History filters do not actually filter
Description (plain English): The search box, zone picker, date range and severity picker look like they work, but the list ignores them and always shows the latest 100 events.
Example Flow: User picks zone 'Adugodi' and last week -> the list still shows the newest 100 events from everywhere.
Expected Outcome: The list shows only events matching the chosen zone, dates and severity.

Title: Two cards show numbers nobody calculates
Description (plain English): The 'Average Response' and 'Resolution Status' cards display values that no part of the system actually works out, so they are blank or zero.
Example Flow: User opens Analytics -> 'Average Response' shows nothing meaningful.
Expected Outcome: Either the numbers are really calculated, or the cards are removed. No card shows a made-up value.
